ai-at-work.title: Microsoft releases new Nvidia-chip AI PCs with revamped Windows 11
ai-at-work.excerpt: Microsoft revealed the specs and price for its Surface Laptop Ultra, AI PCs that run on Nvidia chips that are designed to run AI models and agents.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Microsoft just dropped the Surface Laptop Ultra, a new AI PC line powered by Nvidia chips that can actually run substantial AI models locally instead of just talking about it. This matters because digital workplace teams are finally getting hardware that might make AI tools feel less like cloud-dependent party tricks and more like genuinely useful productivity features. Here's the thing though: most organizations are still figuring out what problems AI actually solves for their people, so buying expensive new machines before that conversation happens is putting the cart about five miles ahead of the horse.

ai-at-work.title: Meta rolls out new AI tools to detect ads that secretly lead to child sexual abuse material
ai-at-work.excerpt: Meta launches new AI tools after discovering ads on its platforms that may look normal but direct users to harmful content elsewhere online.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Meta deployed AI detection tools to catch deceptive ads that appear innocent but actually funnel people toward child exploitation material. This matters to digital workplace pros because it highlights how AI moderation is becoming table stakes for any platform handling user safety, and it's a reminder that your content governance strategy needs teeth. Look, if Meta with all its resources is just now getting serious about this, the rest of us probably need to have a long look in the mirror about what's actually running on our networks.

ai-at-work.title: Google experiments with an AI-powered gaming platform
ai-at-work.excerpt: Google Labs is working on a new AI-powered game-creation platform called Playground for users to build browser-based games using simple text prompts.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Google is building Playground, an AI tool that lets people create browser-based games by typing text prompts instead of writing code. This matters to digital workplace folks because it shows how AI is collapsing the skill gap between idea and execution, which means your non-technical teams could soon build actual applications without waiting for IT. Honestly, if this works half as well as the marketing suggests, we're about three months away from someone's boss asking why the entire marketing department doesn't just build their own internal tools now.

tools-tech.title: Managers are using AI to write performance reviews – and it shows
tools-tech.excerpt: Does AI use help or hurt feedback at work? Here’s what one survey found.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Managers are increasingly using AI tools to draft performance reviews instead of writing them from scratch themselves. This matters because the quality of feedback directly impacts employee development, retention, and morale, and AI-generated reviews often lack the personal context and specificity that make feedback actually useful. Look, if your manager can't be bothered to spend thirty minutes thinking about your actual performance, handing it off to ChatGPT probably isn't going to result in feedback that helps you grow.

tools-tech.title: Cisco brings collaborative agents and Claude into Webex chats
tools-tech.excerpt: Cisco is adding AI agents to Webex group chats so colleagues can assign them work and share the results, part of a wider revamp of the Webex app. Announced at the WebexOne conference Wednesday, users
tools-tech.dwp_take: Cisco is embedding AI agents directly into Webex chat so teams can delegate tasks like scheduling and note-taking without leaving the conversation. This matters because it's solving a real problem: AI work happening in isolation while teammates stay in the dark, which defeats the whole point of collaboration. Finally, someone's building AI tools that live where actual work happens instead of expecting people to juggle seventeen different windows like it's 2015.

tools-tech.title: LibreOffice touts ‘no AI’ as a feature
tools-tech.excerpt: The lack of artificial intelligence features in LibreOffice should be considered a feature in and of itself, according to the free office suite’s creators. The Document Foundation, the organization be
tools-tech.dwp_take: LibreOffice is marketing the absence of AI features as a deliberate choice rather than a limitation. This matters because it highlights a growing divide in how vendors position their products, with some users actively seeking tools that don't collect data or depend on cloud-based AI processing. I'd say this is smart positioning for a segment that's tired of AI being shoved into every corner of their software, though let's be honest: they'll probably add it eventually anyway.

tools-tech.title: How to navigate the Windows Insider Program
tools-tech.excerpt: Are you a Windows fan? Do you like getting sneak peeks at features before they’re released to the public? Microsoft created its Windows Insider Program for you. The program made its debut in October 2
tools-tech.dwp_take: Computerworld ran a piece explaining how to get into Microsoft's Windows Insider Program, which lets users test new Windows features before public release. For digital workplace folks, this matters because testing early builds helps you understand what's coming down the pipe and catch problems before they hit your entire user base. Honestly, it's the smart play if you're responsible for Windows deployments, though fair warning: early builds can be buggy enough to make you question your life choices at 2 AM.

digital-culture.title: As companies spend more on AI, many spend less on workers
digital-culture.excerpt: As organizations race to adopt AI, some are investing in workforce development to complement the technology, while others are shifting resources to tech—and away from people. According to a recent stu
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are cutting jobs and slashing workforce development budgets while dumping money into AI tools. This matters because digital workplace professionals suddenly find themselves building infrastructure for technology that's actively replacing their colleagues, which makes it hard to champion adoption when people are watching their coworkers get pink slips. It's the classic corporate move: spend millions on AI while treating your people like yesterday's tech stack, then act shocked when engagement scores tank and your best people leave for companies that actually value them.

digital-culture.title: Young workers are turning toward AI-proof jobs
digital-culture.excerpt: Entry level jobs are an endangered animal, at least in professions exposed to disruption from AI. While new grads are still seeing opportunities in fields like real estate, utilities, and construction
digital-culture.dwp_take: Young college graduates are increasingly avoiding careers vulnerable to AI automation and gravitating toward jobs in real estate, utilities, and construction instead. This matters to digital workplace pros because it signals a fundamental shift in how organizations need to think about workforce planning, skills development, and the kinds of roles worth investing in training people for. After thirty years watching industries transform, I can tell you this: the companies freaking out about AI replacing workers should be way more worried about the talent pipeline drying up in the first place.

digital-culture.title: Memory loss is not always the first sign of dementia. Doctors say to watch for these 8 eating changes
digital-culture.excerpt: Over six million people in the U.S. live with dementia. By 2050, that number is expected to double. Yet, even so, the signs of cognitive decline can be difficult to spot. Alzheimer’s disease is the mo
digital-culture.dwp_take: Researchers are identifying eight eating behavior changes as early warning signs of dementia, challenging the common assumption that memory loss is always the first indicator. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because undiagnosed cognitive decline in employees or leadership can quietly degrade decision-making, communication, and productivity before anyone realizes there's a problem. The real takeaway: if your CEO suddenly starts ordering five lunches a day or your star performer abandons their usual routine, it might be worth a concerned conversation rather than assuming they've just lost it.

digital-culture.title: Does your workforce have a happiness problem? It may be costing you more than you think
digital-culture.excerpt: I was having lunch recently with a dear colleague I used to work with, reminiscing about our early-2000s days at Rainey Kelly Campbell Roalfe, a creative agency with a generation of alumni who loved w
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company is asking why workplace joy has evaporated compared to the early 2000s, suggesting unhappiness is now a real cost factor for organizations. This matters because digital workplace strategy should create conditions where people actually want to show up, not just where they're forced to log in remotely. Here's the thing though: you can't buy happiness with better collaboration software, and pretending Slack fixes culture problems is exactly how you end up with joyless people just chatting faster.

industry-news.title: Microsoft’s $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra Puts Nvidia RTX Spark Inside a Windows Laptop
industry-news.excerpt: Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599 with an Nvidia RTX Spark GPU, up to 128GB of memory, and support for running large AI models locally. The post Microsoft’s $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra
industry-news.dwp_take: Microsoft released a $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia RTX graphics and up to 128GB of RAM, designed to run large AI models locally on the device. For digital workplace leaders, this signals that organizations can now seriously consider on-device AI processing instead of cloud-dependent solutions, which matters for security, latency, and cost at scale. Here's the thing though: most of your workforce still can't justify a $2,600 laptop, so this is really just Microsoft flexing while IT departments figure out how to explain the price tag to their CFOs.
